title: Installing Wall Sconces in an Older Home: Wiring, Box Reuse, and Fireplace Mounting

locations.name: Living Room / Fireplace Wall
locations.basis: Transcript centers the discussion on lighting in the living room and mounting sconces above the fireplace.

locations.name: Basement
locations.basis: Explicit: they go downstairs to access wiring and plan routing for the sconces.

summary: This This Old House episode follows Kevin and Heath as they troubleshoot and upgrade historical lighting around a living-room fireplace. They evaluate existing, nonfunctional wall switches, locate old plaster sconce boxes behind the fireplace, and determine that new wiring and larger boxes are required for proper, code-compliant sconces. The crew runs wire from the basement to a new wall location, uses a low-profile drilling trick to locate wall cavities, and pulls wires to the new sconces. They relocate a wall switch to a more logical position in the room, install the sconces, and patch the surrounding plaster. Throughout, they reference finding old wall contents (including a 1955 newspaper) as evidence of the wall’s history, and emphasize careful measurement from the mantel to ensure even, aesthetically pleasing sconce heights. The episode emphasizes planning, safe electrical work in an older home, and finishing touches for a clean install.

sections.title: Assessment and goal setting: dark living room, possible sconces over the fireplace
sections.description: The hosts identify that the living room is underlit and that existing floor lamps with a wireless switch are not ideal. They note that sconces over the fireplace are a common feature in similar homes and begin planning toward installing hardwired sconces in that location.

sections.title: Inspecting existing wiring and locating old sconce boxes via switch and wall work
concepts: existing wiring tied to nearby lights
sections.description: The team examines the wall switches, identifies a dead/unused switch, and confirms that the other switches likely feed the existing lighting. They begin to verify the probable sconce box locations behind the plaster near the fireplace.

sections.title: Wiring tracing with toner and confirmation at the fireplace
concepts: confirming wall path from basement to sconces
sections.description: Using a toner and a receiver, Heath traces the wiring from the wall to the sconces, confirming the likely plaster boxes behind the fireplace and establishing the general routing path before making changes.

sections.title: Basement routing, plan for new switch location, and final sconce installation
concepts: drilling strategies and wall cavity access
finding old sconce boxes and upgrading to larger boxes
measuring heights from mantel for alignment
sections.description: The bulk of the project unfolds: they locate a convenient route from the basement, plan a new switch location on a suitable wall, and prepare to route power to the sconces. Heath demonstrates a DIY technique using an insulation tie as a drill-bit starter to locate wall cavities, then they drill up to fish wires through studs, locate the original sconce boxes (including a 1955 newspaper found in the wall), and decide to upgrade to larger boxes. They pull cables from the basement, install a proper switch location, mount the hardwired sconces, and test the system after restoring power. They also emphasize careful plaster work and patching around the old openings.
